verses.text: Where has your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your beloved turn, so that we can look for him with you?
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
I belong to my beloved, and my beloved belongs to me. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
You are beautiful, my love, like the city of Tirzah, lovely like Jerusalem, as stunning as an army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they overwhelm me. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down the slopes of Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing. Each one has its twin, and not one of them is missing.
Your cheeks behind your veil are like halves of a pomegranate.
There may be sixty queens, eighty other wives, and young women without number.

But my dove, my perfect one, is the only one. She is her mother's only daughter, the favorite of the one who gave birth to her. The young women saw her and called her blessed. The queens and the other wives saw her and praised her.
Who is this who appears like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, as stunning as an army with banners?
I went down to the grove of nut trees to look at the new growth in the valley, to see whether the vines had budded and the pomegranates were in bloom.
Before I knew it, my desire had placed me among the royal chariots of my people.
Come back, come back, Shulammite! Come back, come back, so that we may look at you! He says: Why do you want to look at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
